definition: Neurocomputing is a peer-reviewed scientific journal covering research on artificial intelligence, machine learning, and neural computation.
details: It was established in 1989 and is published by Elsevier. The editor-in-chief is Zidong Wang (Brunel University London). Independent scientometric studies noted that despite being one of the most productive journals in the field, it has kept its reputation across the years intact and plays an important role in leading the research in the area. The journal is abstracted and indexed in Scopus and Science Citation Index Expanded. According to the Journal Citation Reports, its 2023 impact factor is 5.5.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Boil it down and it is this: Neurocomputing is a peer-reviewed scientific journal covering research on artificial intelligence, machine learning, and neural computation. Here is why it matters: It was established in 1989 and is published by Elsevier. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. That blueprint is Neurocomputing (journal).
